Rules of engagement.subject: Applied Sciences
Rules of engagement.question: The _____ was Internal limits, authorizations and directives on use of force in combat.
Rules of engagement.fact: Rules of engagement (ROE) are the internal rules or directives afforded military forces (including individuals) that define the circumstances, conditions, degree, and manner in which the use of force, or actions which might be construed as provocative, may be applied. Rules of engagement do not normally dictate how a result is to be achieved, but will indicate what measures may be unacceptable.

Rumi.fact: Jalāl al-Dīn Muḥammad Rūmī (30 September 1207 – 17 December 1273), commonly called Rumi, was a Sufi mystic, poet, and founder of the Islamic brotherhood called the Mevlevi Order. Rumi.fact: Although he was exposed to Sufi thought from his early childhood, he was expected to follow his fathers footsteps as an Islamic scholar.

Rumi.fact: We do not learn the name of Baha al-Din's mother in the sources, only that he referred to her as "Māmi" (colloquial Persian for Māma), and that she was a simple woman who lived to the 1200s.

Rumi.fact: Shams had travelled throughout the Middle East searching and praying for someone who could "endure my company".

Rumi.fact: Shams had travelled throughout the Middle East searching and praying for someone who could "endure my company". A voice said to him: "What will you give in return?" Shams replied, "My head!" The voice then said, "The one you seek is Jalal ud-Din of Konya." On the night of 5 December 1248, as Rumi and Shams were talking, Shams was called to the back door.

Rumi.question: He himself went out searching for Shams and journeyed again to _____
Rumi.fact: He himself went out searching for Shams and journeyed again to Damascus.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences

Rumi.fact: In December 1273, Rumi fell ill; he predicted his own death and composed the well-known ghazal, which begins with the verse: How doest thou know what sort of king I have within me as companion? Do not cast thy glance upon my golden face, for I have iron legs. Rumi died on 17 December 1273 in Konya.

Rumi.fact: She was the one who sponsored the construction of his tomb in Konya.

Rumi.fact: It was from these ideas that the practice of whirling Dervishes developed into a ritual form.

Rumi.fact: The sermons themselves give a commentary on the deeper meaning of Qur'an and Hadith. The style of Persian is rather simple, but quotation of Arabic and knowledge of history and the Hadith show Rumi's knowledge in the Islamic sciences.

Rumi.fact: His style is typical of the genre of lectures given by Sufis and spiritual teachers.

Rumi.question: The Book conveys the prophets' circumstances those fish of the pure sea of _____

Rumi.fact: His poetry influenced not only Persian literature, but also the literary traditions of the Ottoman Turkish, Chagatai, Pashto, Kurdish, Urdu, and Bengali languages.

Saladin.question: In _____, the defeated army of Zengi, Atabeg of Mosul, found their retreat blocked by the Tigris River opposite the fortress of Tikrit, where Saladin's father, Najm ad-Din Ayyub served as the warden
Saladin.fact: In 1132, the defeated army of Zengi, Atabeg of Mosul, found their retreat blocked by the Tigris River opposite the fortress of Tikrit, where Saladin's father, Najm ad-Din Ayyub served as the warden.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Ayyub provided ferries for the army and gave them refuge in _____
Saladin.fact: In 1132, the defeated army of Zengi, Atabeg of Mosul, found their retreat blocked by the Tigris River opposite the fortress of Tikrit, where Saladin's father, Najm ad-Din Ayyub served as the warden. Ayyub provided ferries for the army and gave them refuge in Tikrit.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____, Ayyub and his family moved to Mosul, where Imad ad-Din Zengi acknowledged his debt and appointed Ayyub commander of his fortress in Baalbek
Saladin.fact: In 1139, Ayyub and his family moved to Mosul, where Imad ad-Din Zengi acknowledged his debt and appointed Ayyub commander of his fortress in Baalbek.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: After the death of Zengi in _____, his son, Nur ad-Din, became the regent of Aleppo and the leader of the Zengids
Saladin.fact: After the death of Zengi in 1146, his son, Nur ad-Din, became the regent of Aleppo and the leader of the Zengids.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Another factor which may have affected his interest in religion was that, during the _____, Jerusalem was taken by the Christians
Saladin.fact: Another factor which may have affected his interest in religion was that, during the First Crusade, Jerusalem was taken by the Christians.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: More significantly, he knew the Hamasah of _____ by heart
Saladin.fact: More significantly, he knew the Hamasah of Abu Tammam by heart.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He spoke _____ and Arabic, and knew Turkish and Persian
Saladin.fact: He spoke Kurdish and Arabic, and knew Turkish and Persian.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Above all else he was a devotee of jihad: The sacred works [_____, hadith, etc.] are full of passages referring to the jihad
Saladin.fact: Above all else he was a devotee of jihad: The sacred works [Koran, hadith, etc.] are full of passages referring to the jihad.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____, Saladin ordered the arrest of a Sufi mystic, Qadid al-Qaffas (Arabic: قديد القفاص), in Alexandria
Saladin.fact: In 1174, Saladin ordered the arrest of a Sufi mystic, Qadid al-Qaffas (Arabic: قديد القفاص), in Alexandria.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____, he ordered his son to execute the Sufi philosopher Yahya al-Suhrawardi, the founder of the Illuminationist current in Muslim philosophy, in Aleppo
Saladin.fact: In 1191, he ordered his son to execute the Sufi philosopher Yahya al-Suhrawardi, the founder of the Illuminationist current in Muslim philosophy, in Aleppo.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The answers to these questions lie in the kinds of _____ he wished to attract
Saladin.fact: Saladin welcomed Asiatic Sufis to Egypt, and he and his followers set up and endowed many khanqahs and zawiyas of which al-Maqrizi gives a long list. However, it is not yet clear what Saladin's interests in the khanqah actually were and why he specifically wanted Sufis from outside Egypt.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The founder stipulated that the khanqah be endowed for the Sufis as a group, those coming from abroad and settling in Cairo and _____
Saladin.fact: The founder stipulated that the khanqah be endowed for the Sufis as a group, those coming from abroad and settling in Cairo and Fustat.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: If those could not be found, then it would be for the poor jurists, either Shafi'i or _____, and Ash'ari in their creed
Saladin.fact: If those could not be found, then it would be for the poor jurists, either Shafi'i or Maliki, and Ash'ari in their creed.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____, Shawar, the vizier to al-Adid, who was the Fatimid caliph at the time, had been driven out of Egypt by his rival Dirgham, a member of the powerful Banu Ruzzaik tribe
Saladin.fact: In 1163, Shawar, the vizier to al-Adid, who was the Fatimid caliph at the time, had been driven out of Egypt by his rival Dirgham, a member of the powerful Banu Ruzzaik tribe.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He asked for military backing from Nur ad-Din, who complied, and in _____, sent Shirkuh to aid Shawar in his expedition against Dirgham
Saladin.fact: He asked for military backing from Nur ad-Din, who complied, and in 1164, sent Shirkuh to aid Shawar in his expedition against Dirgham.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: After the sacking of _____, the Crusader–Egyptian force and Shirkuh's army were to engage in the Battle of al-Babein on the desert border of the Nile, just west of Giza
Saladin.fact: Saladin's role in this expedition was minor, and it is known that he was ordered by Shirkuh to collect stores from Bilbais prior to its siege by a combined force of Crusaders and Shawar's troops. After the sacking of Bilbais, the Crusader–Egyptian force and Shirkuh's army were to engage in the Battle of al-Babein on the desert border of the Nile, just west of Giza.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Faced by a superior _____–Egyptian force attempting to besiege the city, Shirkuh split his army
Saladin.fact: Faced by a superior Crusader–Egyptian force attempting to besiege the city, Shirkuh split his army.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____, Shawar was reportedly assassinated by Saladin, and Shirkuh died later that year
Saladin.fact: In 1169, Shawar was reportedly assassinated by Saladin, and Shirkuh died later that year.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Following his death, a number of candidates were considered for the role of vizier to al-_____, most of whom were ethnic Kurds
Saladin.fact: Following his death, a number of candidates were considered for the role of vizier to al-Adid, most of whom were ethnic Kurds.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Their ethnic solidarity came to shape the _____ family's actions in their political career
Saladin.fact: Their ethnic solidarity came to shape the Ayyubid family's actions in their political career.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Having gained more power and independence than ever before in his career, he still faced the issue of ultimate loyalty between al-_____ and Nur ad-Din
Saladin.fact: Having gained more power and independence than ever before in his career, he still faced the issue of ultimate loyalty between al-Adid and Nur ad-Din.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Towards the end of _____, Saladin, with reinforcements from Nur ad-Din, defeated a massive Crusader-Byzantine force near Damietta
Saladin.fact: Towards the end of 1169, Saladin, with reinforcements from Nur ad-Din, defeated a massive Crusader-Byzantine force near Damietta.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: After establishing himself in Egypt, Saladin launched a campaign against the Crusaders, besieging Darum in _____
Saladin.fact: Afterwards, in the spring of 1170, Nur ad-Din sent Saladin's father to Egypt in compliance with Saladin's request, as well as encouragement from the Baghdad-based Abbasid caliph, al-Mustanjid, who aimed to pressure Saladin in deposing his rival caliph, al-Ad. After establishing himself in Egypt, Saladin launched a campaign against the Crusaders, besieging Darum in 1170.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Amalric withdrew his Knights Templar garrison from Gaza to assist him in defending Darum, but Saladin evaded their force and captured Gaza in _____
Saladin.fact: Amalric withdrew his Knights Templar garrison from Gaza to assist him in defending Darum, but Saladin evaded their force and captured Gaza in 1187.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____ Saladin destroyed the fortifications in Gaza built by King Baldwin III for the Knights Templar
Saladin.fact: In 1191 Saladin destroyed the fortifications in Gaza built by King Baldwin III for the Knights Templar.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: It is unclear exactly when, but during that same year, he attacked and captured the _____ castle of Eilat, built on an island off the head of the Gulf of Aqaba
Saladin.fact: After establishing himself in Egypt, Saladin launched a campaign against the Crusaders, besieging Darum in 1170. It is unclear exactly when, but during that same year, he attacked and captured the Crusader castle of Eilat, built on an island off the head of the Gulf of Aqaba.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Several Egyptian emirs were thus killed, but al-_____ was told that they were killed for rebelling against him
Saladin.fact: Several Egyptian emirs were thus killed, but al-Adid was told that they were killed for rebelling against him. While ill, he asked Saladin to pay him a visit to request that he take care of his young children, but Saladin refused, fearing treachery against the Abbasids, and is said to have regretted his action after realizing what al-Adid had wanted.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He died on 13 _____, and five days later, the Abbasid khutba was pronounced in Cairo and al-Fustat, proclaiming al-Mustadi as caliph
Saladin.fact: He died on 13 September, and five days later, the Abbasid khutba was pronounced in Cairo and al-Fustat, proclaiming al-Mustadi as caliph. On 25 September, Saladin left Cairo to take part in a joint attack on Kerak and Montréal, the desert castles of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, with Nur ad-Din who would attack from Syria.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: During the summer of _____, a Nubian army along with a contingent of Armenian former Fatimid troops were reported on the Egyptian border, preparing for a siege against Aswan
Saladin.fact: During the summer of 1173, a Nubian army along with a contingent of Armenian former Fatimid troops were reported on the Egyptian border, preparing for a siege against Aswan. Consequently, the Nubians departed; but returned in 1173 and were again driven off.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Consequently, the Nubians departed; but returned in _____ and were again driven off
Saladin.fact: During the summer of 1173, a Nubian army along with a contingent of Armenian former Fatimid troops were reported on the Egyptian border, preparing for a siege against Aswan. Consequently, the Nubians departed; but returned in 1173 and were again driven off.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: This time, _____ forces advanced from Aswan and captured the Nubian town of Ibrim
Saladin.fact: During the summer of 1173, a Nubian army along with a contingent of Armenian former Fatimid troops were reported on the Egyptian border, preparing for a siege against Aswan. This time, Egyptian forces advanced from Aswan and captured the Nubian town of Ibrim.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He did not press an attack against the desert castles, but attempted to drive out the _____ who lived in Crusader territory with the aim of depriving the Franks of guides
Saladin.fact: He did not press an attack against the desert castles, but attempted to drive out the Muslim Bedouins who lived in Crusader territory with the aim of depriving the Franks of guides.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: On 31 July _____, Saladin's father Ayyub was wounded in a horse-riding accident, ultimately causing his death on 9 August
Saladin.fact: On 31 July 1173, Saladin's father Ayyub was wounded in a horse-riding accident, ultimately causing his death on 9 August.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____, Saladin sent Turan-Shah to conquer Yemen to allocate it and its port Aden to the territories of the Ayyubid Dynasty
Saladin.fact: In 1174, Saladin sent Turan-Shah to conquer Yemen to allocate it and its port Aden to the territories of the Ayyubid Dynasty.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: On 15 May, Nur ad-Din died after falling ill the previous week and his power was handed to his eleven-year-old son as-_____ al-Malik
Saladin.fact: On 15 May, Nur ad-Din died after falling ill the previous week and his power was handed to his eleven-year-old son as-Salih Ismail al-Malik.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: When as-Salih was removed to _____ in August, Gumushtigin, the emir of the city and a captain of Nur ad-Din's veterans assumed guardianship over him
Saladin.fact: When as-Salih was removed to Aleppo in August, Gumushtigin, the emir of the city and a captain of Nur ad-Din's veterans assumed guardianship over him. In this emergency, the emir of Damascus appealed to Saif ad-Din of Mosul (a cousin of Gumushtigin) for assistance against Aleppo, but he refused, forcing the Syrians to request the aid of Saladin, who complied.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The emir prepared to unseat all his rivals in Syria and the Jazira, beginning with _____
Saladin.fact: The emir prepared to unseat all his rivals in Syria and the Jazira, beginning with Damascus. In this emergency, the emir of Damascus appealed to Saif ad-Din of Mosul (a cousin of Gumushtigin) for assistance against Aleppo, but he refused, forcing the Syrians to request the aid of Saladin, who complied.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: His army conquered _____ with relative ease, but avoided attacking Homs because of the strength of its citadel
Saladin.fact: His army conquered Hama with relative ease, but avoided attacking Homs because of the strength of its citadel.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: On 11 May _____, a group of thirteen Assassins easily gained admission into Saladin's camp, but were detected immediately before they carried out their attack by Nasih ad-Din Khumartekin of Abu Qubays
Saladin.fact: On 11 May 1175, a group of thirteen Assassins easily gained admission into Saladin's camp, but were detected immediately before they carried out their attack by Nasih ad-Din Khumartekin of Abu Qubays.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Soon after, Saladin entered Homs and captured its citadel in March _____, after stubborn resistance from its defenders
Saladin.fact: Soon after, Saladin entered Homs and captured its citadel in March 1175, after stubborn resistance from its defenders.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Saif ad-Din mustered a large army and dispatched it to _____, whose defenders anxiously had awaited them
Saladin.fact: Saif ad-Din mustered a large army and dispatched it to Aleppo, whose defenders anxiously had awaited them. The combined forces of Mosul and Aleppo marched against Saladin in Hama.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: On 13 April _____, the Zengid troops marched to attack his forces, but soon found themselves surrounded by Saladin's Ayyubid veterans, who crushed them
Saladin.fact: On 13 April 1175, the Zengid troops marched to attack his forces, but soon found themselves surrounded by Saladin's Ayyubid veterans, who crushed them.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The Battle of Hama did not end the contest for power between the Ayyubids and the Zengids, with the final confrontation occurring in the spring of _____
Saladin.fact: The Battle of Hama did not end the contest for power between the Ayyubids and the Zengids, with the final confrontation occurring in the spring of 1176.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He reached the _____'s Mound, roughly 25 km (16 mi) from Aleppo, where his forces encountered Saif ad-Din's army
Saladin.fact: He reached the Sultan's Mound, roughly 25 km (16 mi) from Aleppo, where his forces encountered Saif ad-Din's army.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The Zengid forces panicked and most of _____ ad-Din's officers ended up being killed or captured—Saif ad-Din narrowly escaped
Saladin.fact: He reached the Sultan's Mound, roughly 25 km (16 mi) from Aleppo, where his forces encountered Saif ad-Din's army. The Zengid forces panicked and most of Saif ad-Din's officers ended up being killed or captured—Saif ad-Din narrowly escaped.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The Zengid army's camp, horses, baggage, tents, and stores were seized by the _____
Saladin.fact: The Zengid army's camp, horses, baggage, tents, and stores were seized by the Ayyubids.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He continued towards _____, which still closed its gates to him, halting before the city
Saladin.fact: He continued towards Aleppo, which still closed its gates to him, halting before the city.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: On the way, his army took Buza'a and then captured _____
Saladin.fact: On the way, his army took Buza'a and then captured Manbij.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The cap of his head armour was not penetrated and he managed to grip the _____'s hand—the dagger only slashing his gambeson—and the assailant was soon killed
Saladin.fact: Several days later, while Saladin was resting in one of his captain's tents, an Assassin rushed forward at him and struck at his head with a knife. The cap of his head armour was not penetrated and he managed to grip the Assassin's hand—the dagger only slashing his gambeson—and the assailant was soon killed.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Based in the an-_____, they commanded nine fortresses, all built on high elevations
Saladin.fact: Based in the an-Nusayriyah Mountains, they commanded nine fortresses, all built on high elevations.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: As soon as he dispatched the bulk of his troops to Egypt, Saladin led his army into the an-Nusayriyah range in August _____
Saladin.fact: As soon as he dispatched the bulk of his troops to Egypt, Saladin led his army into the an-Nusayriyah range in August 1176.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He saw that the lamps were displaced and beside his bed laid hot scones of the shape peculiar to the _____ with a note at the top pinned by a poisoned dagger
Saladin.fact: Saladin had his guards supplied with link lights and had chalk and cinders strewed around his tent outside Masyaf—which he was besieging—to detect any footsteps by the Assassins. He saw that the lamps were displaced and beside his bed laid hot scones of the shape peculiar to the Assassins with a note at the top pinned by a poisoned dagger.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He left _____ in command of Syria and left for Egypt with only his personal followers, reaching Cairo on 22 September
Saladin.fact: He left Turan Shah in command of Syria and left for Egypt with only his personal followers, reaching Cairo on 22 September.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Having been absent for roughly two years, he had much to organize and supervise in _____, namely fortifying and reconstructing Cairo
Saladin.fact: He left Turan Shah in command of Syria and left for Egypt with only his personal followers, reaching Cairo on 22 September. Having been absent for roughly two years, he had much to organize and supervise in Egypt, namely fortifying and reconstructing Cairo.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The city walls were repaired and their extensions laid out, while the construction of the _____ was commenced
Saladin.fact: The city walls were repaired and their extensions laid out, while the construction of the Cairo Citadel was commenced.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The chief public work he commissioned outside of Cairo was the large bridge at Giza, which was intended to form an outwork of defence against a potential _____ invasion
Saladin.fact: The chief public work he commissioned outside of Cairo was the large bridge at Giza, which was intended to form an outwork of defence against a potential Moorish invasion.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In November _____, he set out upon a raid into Palestine; the Crusaders had recently forayed into the territory of Damascus, so Saladin saw the truce as no longer worth preserving
Saladin.fact: In November 1177, he set out upon a raid into Palestine; the Crusaders had recently forayed into the territory of Damascus, so Saladin saw the truce as no longer worth preserving.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The Christians sent a large portion of their army to besiege the fortress of Harim north of Aleppo, so southern _____ bore few defenders
Saladin.fact: In November 1177, he set out upon a raid into Palestine; the Crusaders had recently forayed into the territory of Damascus, so Saladin saw the truce as no longer worth preserving. The Christians sent a large portion of their army to besiege the fortress of Harim north of Aleppo, so southern Palestine bore few defenders.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: William of Tyre recorded that the _____ army consisted of 26,000 soldiers, of which 8,000 were elite forces and 18,000 were black soldiers from Sudan
Saladin.fact: William of Tyre recorded that the Ayyubid army consisted of 26,000 soldiers, of which 8,000 were elite forces and 18,000 were black soldiers from Sudan. On 25 November, while the greater part of the Ayyubid army was absent, Saladin and his men were surprised near Ramla in the battle of Montgisard (possibly at Gezer, also called Tell Jezar).

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: This army proceeded to raid the countryside, sack Ramla and Lod, and disperse themselves as far as the Gates of _____
Saladin.fact: This army proceeded to raid the countryside, sack Ramla and Lod, and disperse themselves as far as the Gates of Jerusalem.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Before they could form up, the _____ force hacked the soldiers of the Ayyubid army down by sword
Saladin.fact: Although the Crusader force consisted of only 375 knights, Saladin hesitated to ambush them because of the presence of highly skilled templar generals. Before they could form up, the Templar force hacked the soldiers of the Ayyubid army down by sword.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In the spring of _____, he was encamped under the walls of Homs, and a few skirmishes occurred between his generals and the Crusader army
Saladin.fact: In the spring of 1178, he was encamped under the walls of Homs, and a few skirmishes occurred between his generals and the Crusader army.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He spent the rest of the year in _____ without a confrontation with his enemies
Saladin.fact: He spent the rest of the year in Syria without a confrontation with his enemies. Saladin's intelligence services reported to him that the Crusaders were planning a raid into Syria.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In April _____, the Crusaders and Templars led by King Baldwin expected no resistance and waited to launch a surprise attack on Muslim herders grazing their herds and flocks east of the Golan Heights
Saladin.fact: In April 1179, the Crusaders and Templars led by King Baldwin expected no resistance and waited to launch a surprise attack on Muslim herders grazing their herds and flocks east of the Golan Heights. In the summer of 1179, King Baldwin had set up an outpost on the road to Damascus and aimed to fortify a passage over the Jordan River, called Jacob's Ford, that commanded the approach to the Banias plain (the plain was divided by the Muslims and the Christians).

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Baldwin advanced too rashly in pursuit of _____-Shah's force, which was concentrated southeast of Quneitra and was subsequently defeated by the Ayyubids
Saladin.fact: He ordered one of his generals, Farrukh-Shah, to guard the Damascus frontier with a thousand of his men to watch for an attack, then to retire, avoiding battle, and to light warning beacons on the hills, after which Saladin would march out. Baldwin advanced too rashly in pursuit of Farrukh-Shah's force, which was concentrated southeast of Quneitra and was subsequently defeated by the Ayyubids.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He then resolved to destroy the fortress, called "_____" and defended by the Templar knights, moving his headquarters to Banias
Saladin.fact: He then resolved to destroy the fortress, called "Chastellet" and defended by the Templar knights, moving his headquarters to Banias.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: As the _____ hurried down to attack the Muslim forces, they fell into disorder, with the infantry falling behind
Saladin.fact: As the Crusaders hurried down to attack the Muslim forces, they fell into disorder, with the infantry falling behind. Despite early success, they pursued the Muslims far enough to become scattered, and Saladin took advantage by rallying his troops and charging at the Crusaders.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The engagement ended in a decisive _____ victory, and many high-ranking knights were captured
Saladin.fact: The engagement ended in a decisive Ayyubid victory, and many high-ranking knights were captured.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Saladin then moved to besiege the fortress, which fell on 30 August _____
Saladin.fact: Saladin then moved to besiege the fortress, which fell on 30 August 1179.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In the spring of _____, while Saladin was in the area of Safad, anxious to commence a vigorous campaign against the Kingdom of Jerusalem, King Baldwin sent messengers to him with proposals of peace
Saladin.fact: In the spring of 1180, while Saladin was in the area of Safad, anxious to commence a vigorous campaign against the Kingdom of Jerusalem, King Baldwin sent messengers to him with proposals of peace.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: This was intended to cement an alliance with the _____ and to impress other emirs in Mesopotamia and Anatolia
Saladin.fact: This was intended to cement an alliance with the Artuqids and to impress other emirs in Mesopotamia and Anatolia.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The latter demanded that Nur ad-Din return the lands given to him as a dowry for marrying his daughter when he received reports that she was being abused and used to gain _____ territory
Saladin.fact: Previously, Saladin offered to mediate relations between Nur ad-Din and Kilij Arslan II—the Seljuk sultan of Rûm—after the two came into conflict. The latter demanded that Nur ad-Din return the lands given to him as a dowry for marrying his daughter when he received reports that she was being abused and used to gain Seljuk territory.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He threatened to attack the city of _____, saying, "it is two days march for me and I shall not dismount [my horse] until I am in the city." Alarmed at the threat, the Seljuks pushed for negotiations
Saladin.fact: He threatened to attack the city of Malatya, saying, "it is two days march for me and I shall not dismount [my horse] until I am in the city." Alarmed at the threat, the Seljuks pushed for negotiations.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Leaving Farrukh-Shah in charge of Syria, Saladin returned to Cairo at the beginning of _____
Saladin.fact: Leaving Farrukh-Shah in charge of Syria, Saladin returned to Cairo at the beginning of 1181.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: According to _____, he intended to spend the fast of Ramadan in Egypt and then make the hajj pilgrimage to Mecca in the summer
Saladin.fact: According to Abu Shama, he intended to spend the fast of Ramadan in Egypt and then make the hajj pilgrimage to Mecca in the summer.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: For an unknown reason, he apparently changed his plans regarding the pilgrimage and was seen inspecting the _____ banks in June
Saladin.fact: For an unknown reason, he apparently changed his plans regarding the pilgrimage and was seen inspecting the Nile River banks in June.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He was again embroiled with the _____; he removed two-thirds of their fiefs to use as compensation for the fief-holders at Fayyum
Saladin.fact: He was again embroiled with the Bedouin; he removed two-thirds of their fiefs to use as compensation for the fief-holders at Fayyum. The Bedouin were also accused of trading with the Crusaders and, consequently, their grain was confiscated and they were forced to migrate westward.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The Bedouin were also accused of trading with the _____ and, consequently, their grain was confiscated and they were forced to migrate westward
Saladin.fact: The Bedouin were also accused of trading with the Crusaders and, consequently, their grain was confiscated and they were forced to migrate westward.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Later, _____ warships were deployed against Bedouin river pirates, who were plundering the shores of Lake Tanis
Saladin.fact: Later, Ayyubid warships were deployed against Bedouin river pirates, who were plundering the shores of Lake Tanis.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He had _____ ad-Din released in return for a payment of 80,000 dinars
Saladin.fact: In the summer of 1181, Saladin's former palace administrator Baha ad-Din Qaraqush led a force to arrest Majd ad-Din—a former deputy of Turan-Shah in the Yemeni town of Zabid—while he was entertaining Imad ad-Din al-Ishfahani at his estate in Cairo. Saladin's intimates accused Majd ad-Din of misappropriating the revenues of Zabid, but Saladin himself believed there was no evidence to back the allegations.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The controversial detainment of _____ ad-Din was a part of the larger discontent associated with the aftermath of Turan-Shah's departure from Yemen
Saladin.fact: Saladin's intimates accused Majd ad-Din of misappropriating the revenues of Zabid, but Saladin himself believed there was no evidence to back the allegations. He had Majd ad-Din released in return for a payment of 80,000 dinars.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Although his deputies continued to send him revenues from the province, centralized authority was lacking and an internal quarrel arose between Izz ad-_____ of Aden and Hittan of Zabid
Saladin.fact: Although his deputies continued to send him revenues from the province, centralized authority was lacking and an internal quarrel arose between Izz ad-Din Uthman of Aden and Hittan of Zabid.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: On 4 _____, the crown prince of the Zengids, as-Salih, died in Aleppo
Saladin.fact: On 4 December, the crown prince of the Zengids, as-Salih, died in Aleppo.
